format: A connected text with gaps. To the right of each line is a CAPITALISED key word — put it into the correct grammatical form: verb tense and voice, non-finite forms, comparative/superlative of adjectives and adverbs, plural nouns, pronouns, numerals.
scoring: Tasks 19–24, 1 point each. Spelling counts — a correct form spelt wrong gets 0.
strategy: Read the whole sentence (and the neighbouring ones) first — the form depends on tense and meaning.
Decide the part of speech and what's needed: verb → tense/voice; adjective → comparison; noun → plural; pronoun → case.
Watch time markers (yesterday, already, since) and passive signals (by, is/are done).
Don't get stuck — mark a hard gap, move on and come back.
Write the FULL form and mind the spelling (doubled letters, -ied, irregular verbs).
common_mistakes: Wrong tense — ignoring time markers or the sequence of tenses.
Active vs passive mixed up.
Irregular verb forms spelt incorrectly.
Forgetting the plural or the third-person -s.
time: 6–8 minutes for both grammar/vocabulary blocks. Don't linger on one gap.

format: Two parts. Word formation (25–29): build a related word from the CAPITALISED key word using prefixes/suffixes (including negatives un-, in-, im-, dis-). Vocabulary (30–36): choose one of four words that fits the collocation and meaning.
scoring: 1 point per gap. Spelling matters in word formation.
strategy: Word formation: first decide the part of speech needed (noun/adjective/adverb/verb), then the right affix.
Check the meaning — if it's negative, add un-/in-/im-/dis-.
Vocabulary: choose by collocation (which word goes with the others), not by guessing.
Re-read the sentence with your word — does it sound natural and fit the grammar?
common_mistakes: Right root but wrong part of speech.
Missing a needed negative prefix.
Spelling errors in the new word.
Vocabulary: picking a synonym that doesn't collocate.
time: 6–8 minutes. Do word formation thoughtfully — that's where mistakes hide.

format: Three formats. Headings: match texts to headings (one heading is extra). Gapped text: insert sentence-parts into the gaps (one part is extra) — it tests coherence. Multiple choice: read a long text and choose the best answer for each question.
strategy: Headings: read each text's main idea and match the gist — don't get hooked by a repeated word.
Gapped text: use the links around the gap (pronouns, this/such, connectors) to find the right part.
Multiple choice: find the place in the text that answers the question — the answer is paraphrased, not copied.
Eliminate options that say more or less than the text actually does.
common_mistakes: Matching by a single repeated word instead of by meaning.
Forgetting the extra heading / extra part.
Multiple choice: picking an option that's true in general but not stated in the text.
time: About 30 minutes. Headings fast (5–7 min); spend the rest on the gapped text and multiple choice.

format: You get an extract from a pen-friend's email on a topic. Write a reply: answer ALL their questions AND ask 3 questions of your own on the given subject. 100–140 words, informal style.
scoring: Max 6 points: K1 task (all answers + your 3 questions + politeness + style), K2 organisation, K3 language. Under 90 words → 0. If K1=0 → the whole task is 0.
strategy: Answer every question in the extract fully. It's a BASIC-level task — you do NOT need to paraphrase; reusing the wording from the prompt is fine and safer.
Ask 3 SPECIFIC questions on the stated subject — not vague 'What about…?', no duplicates, nothing already answered in the extract.
Politeness: thank for the letter + hope for future contact — use 'Hope to hear FROM you' / 'Write back soon' (NOT 'hear you'; 'I look forward to hearing from you' is too formal for a friend).
Informal style: contractions, simple linkers, an opening, a friendly closing and your first name only. No address or date in an e-mail.
Use paragraphs and linking words (K2). Aim for ~115–130 words.
Even if all answers are there, many language errors that blur meaning lower K1 too — keep it clean.
common_mistakes: Not asking 3 questions, or asking vague 'What about…?' questions.
Missing one of the friend's questions.
'Hope to hear you' instead of 'hear from you'; a closing that's too formal.
Formal style, or wrong length (under 90 words = 0).
time: ~20 minutes: 2–3 min plan, 12–13 min writing, 4–5 min check.

task: Opinion text based on a chart (task 38)
format: A project write-up based on a SURVEY. You get a project topic and a table or pie chart with survey results. Structure (5 content aspects + neutral style, 200–250 words): 1) intro — the project, the topic, that you found a SURVEY, the country and the format (table/chart); 2) 2–3 facts with figures tied to the question the respondents were asked; 3) 1–2 comparisons WITH a developed comment; 4) a realistic problem + a concrete solution; 5) your opinion (I think / In my opinion) with a reason.
scoring: Max 14 across 5 criteria (K1 task, K2 organisation, K3 vocabulary, K4 grammar, K5 spelling & punctuation). If K1=0 → the whole task is 0. Copying ≥30% from the prompt → 0. Length 200–250 words.
strategy: Intro must name the SURVEY as the data source + the country + the format (table/pie chart), and it is YOUR project — 'I', never 'we', and never say you made the survey.
Give 2–3 figures tied to the question the respondents were asked; write 'of THE students / the respondents' (with the article) and 'a survey', not 'opinion polls'.
A comparison needs a comparative structure (while/whereas/twice as many…) AND a developed comment — two facts side by side or a bare 'Surprisingly' is not enough.
Give a realistic problem and a concrete solution (not 'the government must solve it'); never invent data that isn't in the chart.
State your opinion explicitly with a marker (I think / In my opinion) + a reason.
One paragraph per aspect; use 'they' (not 'he') for a student/everyone; start with 'Doing a project… / While doing…' (NOT 'While I was doing'); the apostrophe counts as punctuation.
common_mistakes: Intro without the survey source / country / format, or 'we' instead of 'I'.
Two facts side by side with no comparative structure or no comment.
A vague solution ('the government must…') or inventing data not in the chart.
Opinion with no marker (no 'I think / In my opinion') or no reason.
'opinion polls', '50% of students' (missing 'the'), 'While I was doing a project'.
time: 30–35 minutes: 5 min plan, 20–22 min writing, 5–7 min check.

format: Task 1: match 6 speakers (A–F) to statements 1–7 (one extra). Task 2: a dialogue — mark 7 statements (A–G) True / False / Not stated. Tasks 3–9: multiple choice on an interview/monologue. You hear each recording twice.
scoring: 1 point per item (Task 1: 6, Task 2: 7, Tasks 3–9: 7) = 20 points.
strategy: Use the 30 seconds before each recording to read the statements/questions and predict.
Task 1: catch each speaker's MAIN idea, not a single matching word; one statement is extra.
Task 2 (True/False/Not stated): True = the text confirms it; False = the text says the opposite; Not stated = the text gives no basis to judge. Don't use your own knowledge.
The most common trap is False vs Not stated — if you can't find it in the text at all, it's Not stated.
Tasks 3–9: the right option is a paraphrase, not the exact words you hear.
Use the second listening to check the answers you were unsure about.
common_mistakes: Confusing False and Not stated.
Matching by a single repeated word instead of the whole idea (Task 1).
Choosing the option that repeats words from the audio (Tasks 3–9).
Forgetting that one statement in Task 1 is extra.
time: ≈30 minutes for the whole section — the recording sets the pace, no need to rush. Use the pauses.
